summary: US-P2: A price resolves deterministically through the hierarchy, with visible provenance
description:
**As** an organizer, **I want** a price to resolve through venue → series → event → slot → ticket type with explicit overrides, **so that** I can set a house rule once and bend it where I need to — and always see which level won.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** TKT-150 (rule/conflict/provenance shape decided)

This is TKT-5's headline COS: *a price resolves deterministically through the hierarchy with visible provenance (which level won)*. Static time-invariant rules only — the time-windowed tiers are TKT-152, and the sale path is TKT-153.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A migration adds the price-rule storage in the shape TKT-150 decided: `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002), money as integer minor units + ISO-4217 (ADR-001), one row per (scope level, scope id, ticket-type selector). Plain `CREATE INDEX` (ADR-020).
- [ ] Resolution is **deterministic and total**: for any (ticket type, resolution context) exactly one rule wins, or none does and the ticket type's own `price_amount` is the answer — **existing data with no rules resolves to today's price, unchanged**.
- [ ] The default order is most-specific-wins; a rule marked as an **explicit override** inverts that for its subtree, per TKT-150's conflict semantics. Two rules at the same level resolve by the documented tie-break, never by row order or `ORDER BY` luck.
- [ ] The resolution reports **provenance**: the winning rule's id and scope level, and the levels that were considered and lost. A test asserts the losing levels are reported, not just the winner — 'which level won' is unverifiable without them.
- [ ] Catalog exposes resolution over its API; OpenAPI regenerated **and committed before the gate runs** (ADR-009), the operation covered in `services/catalog/internal/api/coverage_test.go` (ADR-030 — catalog is out of the smoke gate), and the public read declares its ADR-004 TTL tier with rationale.
- [ ] The rule lookup is **index-backed**: two tests per ADR-019 — the result is scoped, *and* the scan is (an `EXPLAIN`-level assertion, not just the returned rows).
- [ ] Unit tests cover: each scope level winning in turn, an override inverting the order, the same-level tie-break, and the no-rule fallback.

Quality gates: `make check` green (lint + unit + integration, mirrors CI); contract tests for any touched service boundary (OpenAPI drift check, ADR-009); public-read stories declare their ADR-004 TTL tier with rationale; entities `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002); money is integer minor units + ISO-4217 code, floats banned (ADR-001).

objective.note: Organizers set pricing policy at the level it belongs to and override it locally; today the only price is a flat per-ticket-type amount.

scope.note: IN: rule storage, deterministic resolution, provenance, catalog read endpoint. OUT: time windows (TKT-152), commerce wiring (TKT-153), fees/promos/taxes (TKT-6/TKT-32), back-office UI.

uncertainties.note: The exact rule/conflict shape is TKT-150's output; this ticket's ACs cite it rather than pre-empt it. Per decomposition.md § spike-amended scope, re-sync these ACs to the spike's decision before this ticket reaches Ready.

approach.note: New migration in services/catalog/internal/store/migrations/; resolver as a pure function over loaded rules (the test seam — table-driven, no DB); postgres.go does the scoped fetch; api/server.go exposes it. Mirrors the existing store/postgres/api split.

first_slice.note: Static hierarchy resolution end-to-end (schema → resolver → API → tests) is demoable alone: post rules at two levels, read back which won.

success.note: COS-1 of TKT-5, proven by the loser-reporting test and the no-rule-fallback test.

context_memo.note: Baked below; governingAdrs resolved from docs/adr/ at 2026-07-30 and to be re-resolved at claim time.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code — floats are banned on money paths.
Commit regenerated code (openapi_gen.go, api-types.gen.ts) before running the gate — check-generate diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.
Every public read endpoint declares its ADR-004 TTL tier from birth.

governingAdrs.why: Money on every pricing path is integer minor units + ISO-4217 code; a percentage/discount rule must not introduce a float or a rounding-by-float step.

Catalog owns **rule definitions**; commerce owns **pricing evaluation at sale time**. Do not put rule CRUD in commerce, and do not put cart/fee/promo evaluation in catalog (docs/architecture.md service table).
Contract-first: the OpenAPI document is the source of truth, regenerate `openapi_gen.go` / `api-types.gen.ts` and commit them BEFORE running the gate (check-generate diffs against HEAD).

Migrations run out-of-band via the binary's `migrate` subcommand as a one-shot Compose job; the server path never migrates. New migration files follow the existing numbering in `services/<svc>/internal/store/migrations/`.
Any public read this story adds declares a volatility TTL tier with rationale. A resolved price is availability-adjacent, not seat-map-stable — argue the tier, don't copy one.
A scoped read is only scoped if an index backs the filter. Proving it takes TWO tests: the result is scoped *and* the scan is (plan assertion, not just output).
Plain `CREATE INDEX` — `CONCURRENTLY` is still NOT adopted; preconditions (2) and (3) remain false even after ADR-022. Do not 'improve' this.

Catalog is deliberately OUT of the smoke happy-path coverage gate; its per-operation coverage gate is `services/catalog/internal/api/coverage_test.go`. A new catalog operation must be exercised THERE, not in the smoke suite.
Series/season grouping is the hierarchy level between venue and event — reuse the existing `series`/`seasons` shape, don't invent a parallel grouping.

reference.summary: Today's price is a single `price_amount` column on `ticket_types` (migration 0001); commerce reads it via catalog's `/internal/ticket-types/{id}`.
ADR-019's worked examples (TKT-53, TKT-60) are the shape of the scoping evidence this ticket owes.
